workflow_steps.objective: Confirm business goals, audience, brand scope, SKU range, packaging formats, channels, constraints, success criteria, approvals and missing inputs.
Study the intended customers, retail context, bakery category, competitors, cultural considerations and relevant packaging requirements once markets are confirmed.
Establish positioning and design principles for brand recognition, product appetite, shelf clarity, SKU navigation, accessibility and production feasibility.
Define each pack format, dimensions, material assumptions, information hierarchy, content architecture and relationships across the retail line.
Develop meaningfully different identity-and-packaging directions, showing how each could operate across representative SKUs.
Compare directions against the agreed principles and obtain an explicit client choice before detailed development.
Create or validate cutting, folding, sealing, bleed and safe-area geometry using confirmed converter specifications.
Produce rough physical prototypes to test assembly, fit, handling, visibility, hierarchy, legibility and representative shelf performance.
Apply approved feedback and prototype findings to the chosen identity, packaging structure and information system.
Codify the approved logo, typography, colour, imagery, graphic language, hierarchy and usage rules.
Extend the approved system across all confirmed SKUs with controlled differentiation and consistent mandatory information.
Prepare print-ready masters using confirmed dielines, colour spaces, inks, finishes, trapping, overprint, barcodes and prepress requirements.

missing_inputs: Confirmed brand name, ownership, story, positioning, values and whether any existing identity elements must be retained.
Target customers, sales channels, geographic markets, languages and intended shelf or display context.
Complete initial SKU list, variants, product dimensions, weights, shelf-life needs and differentiation priorities.
Required packaging formats, pack dimensions, product-contact and barrier requirements, opening or resealing needs, and shipping constraints.
Approved ingredients, allergen statements, nutrition data, net quantities, storage instructions, claims, manufacturer details and other market-specific mandatory copy.
Final product names, descriptions, tone of voice, photography or illustration needs, and translation responsibilities.
Barcode data, certification marks, recycling labels and evidence supporting any nutritional, provenance or sustainability claims.
Printer or converter dielines, materials, print processes, colour limits, finishes, tolerances, trapping and prepress specifications.
Budget, quantities, minimum order constraints, sustainability targets, schedule, approval owners and number of review rounds.
Required final file formats, naming conventions, editable-source expectations, mockup scope and handoff destination.
Trademark clearance status and licensing or usage rights for supplied fonts, imagery and other brand assets.
assumptions: The assignment is treated as a net-new or materially redesigned identity and packaging system unless retained assets are identified during intake.
The small retail line is assumed to contain multiple related SKUs that need a scalable differentiation system.
Identity and packaging will be developed as one coordinated system, with representative SKUs used during concept selection before full rollout.
Physical structures may use either stock formats or custom geometry; the choice remains provisional until budget, product and converter requirements are known.
The client and relevant specialists will supply or approve legally compliant product information, claims and barcode data.
The references are treated only as visible evidence of a published identity presentation and apparel application, not as a style directive or evidence of an undisclosed workflow.
stop_conditions: Do not select or refine a direction without an explicit decision from the authorized client approver.
Do not finalize structural packaging or dielines until product dimensions, material requirements and converter specifications are confirmed.
Do not expand the full SKU family until a representative identity-and-packaging direction and differentiation logic are approved.
Do not release production masters while mandatory copy, allergens, nutrition data, claims, translations, barcodes or legal approvals remain provisional.
Do not release print-ready files without confirmed printer profiles, ink and finish constraints, tolerances, bleed, trapping and overprint requirements.
Do not deliver final assets until prototype or proof issues are resolved and the authorized stakeholders approve both design and production content.
rationale: The brief is classified as concept_to_production because it explicitly spans identity creation, packaging-system development, physical validation, production preparation and final delivery. The workflow creates the core system on representative packs before expanding it across the SKU family, with explicit approval and manufacturing gates.
